curriculum.text: use proper formation patterns to write letters

parts.title: Colour each picture that starts with the /s/ sound.
Read these words. Sound them out.
What this worksheet teaches
parts.text: Children learn that the letter s makes its sound. They form the letter, listen for the sound at the start of words, and read short words.

parts.title: How to lead it (about 15 minutes)
text: 1. Say the /s/ sound together; the keyword is sock.
2. Model writing S and s; children trace and write.
3. Name each picture; children colour the ones that begin with the sound.
4. Read the bottom words together, blending the sounds.

parts.title: Answer key
text: Pictures that start with /s/: sock, sun, sand. (Not: apple, top.)

parts.title: Ontario curriculum link (official wording)
text: A2.2 — use proper formation patterns to write letters.
In plain terms: children form the letter the correct way.
In plain terms: children match a letter to the sound it makes.

parts.title: If children get stuck — and ways to adjust
text: Watch for: sounding out s part by part. Cover the rest of the word and say the target first.
Make it easier: do fewer items together first; you read, the child echoes.
Make it harder: ask the child to think of or write one more word with the target.
You'll know it worked when: the child reads the page smoothly and spots the target on sight.
